Actin is the primary protein component of microfilaments, which are part of the cytoskeleton and involved in cell movement and structure. Phalloidin specifically binds actin and prevents its depolymerization, so microfilaments would be most directly affected. Intermediate filaments, collagen fibers, and microtubules are composed of different proteins (e.g., keratin, collagen, tubulin) and would not be directly disrupted by an actin-binding toxin.  

Final answer: (C)
